author: Ifmyante
text:
Until today I hadn't even considered waiting lists, but the number of
people registering their interest has been a surprise, to say the least!

As it is, those who registered their interest first will be given first refusal of a place.

We hope to have our class all signed up and registered by the end of the
 month. Then we'll know what the demand is like, and we'll know when to
schedule the next class after that.

I imagine the Academy will be around for six months to two years. Once
we've enough traders to manage the fund 24/5, we intend to shut it down
until our traders need do it no more, and we're looking for fresh blood
 :)

author: Ifmyante
text:
Here are some great questions I got via pm today:

Hey If.

I have a few questions about the course if you don't mind.

You have said the interest from members has been good. When will
individual members be told they can do this next course or will have to
wait for the following one..?

For the March course what date does the 10K have to be paid by..?

What form of payment methods are available..?

Will the webinars be recorded if we can't make it for the live one..?

Thanks for your time.

We're still unsure of how much interest will turn into actual
registration, so right now I'm afraid we can't answer your first
question with any conviction.

For a definite place in the next class, all registration should be
completed by the 28th of February. By that date we should be in a much
better position to answer your first question :)

Bank draft and bank wire transfer are the preferred payment methods. I
told Paypal I'd never work with those extortionists again, but I suppose
 if any registrants want to give a fortune to them, I suppose we'll have
 to allow it. I'm not familiar with Visa, but I suppose we can offer it
as a payment method like Paypal (ie the registrant covers the cost of
the transfer)

All the webinars will be recorded. For anybody who will or won't be
attending, there's a "Questions for next Webinar" thread, where students
 can set down their queries before the webinar, and be confident they'll
 be addressed in the meeting.

We have me in Dublin and another teacher in Australia, so we can hopefully soon arrange the classes by time-zone.

I look forward to any further questions, as we want to write a complete FAQ

author: Ifmyante
text:
I've been doing a lot of thinking about people who give up everything
to focus their lives on becoming traders, and have come to a very firm
conclusion:

A future in trading can be greatly compromised in the learning stage by needing to win to survive.

I'd advise everybody who's learning to trade to have a source of income
all the way through the process, and not to trade live until you're at
one with the market.

It's only once you're truly at one with the market that stress doesn't
come into your trading. You CAN become one with the markets by learning
in your free time.

A dead-end job is the perfect companion for a trading student. It pays
the bills, but once your shift is over, can be instantly forgotten. If
it's menial, all the better; you can daydream of your studies while you
work.

There's no stigma to be attached to it - it's an easy way to support yourself while you improve your life immeasurably.
